rationale: Across published cohorts and clinical aggregations of FBXO11-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #618089), major structural congenital malformations, specifically complex congenital heart defects (HP:0001627) and congenital limb-reduction deficiencies (HP:0002814), have near-zero penetrance. In the landmark cohort of 20 individuals by Gregor et al. (2018), physical anomalies were restricted to cleft lip/palate or bifid uvula (3/20) and minor skeletal anomalies, with 0/20 exhibiting complex heart defects or limb reductions. Subsequent expanded cohorts and database registries confirm that major congenital anomalies are infrequent; cardiac anomalies occur in very rare instances and are predominantly minor structural variants (e.g., bicuspid aortic valve, reported in 4 individuals in an expanded series of 21 patients, and noted as 'very rare' in Human Disease Genes), leading to a RED rating on the Australian PanelApp Adult Cardiac panel. Limb-reduction defects have not been observed in any assessed FBXO11 cohort. This provides high-confidence negative discrimination against phenotypically overlapping differential diagnoses such as Cornelia de Lange syndrome (where upper-limb reduction defects and structural CHDs are common) and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome.

evidence.text: In a foundational cohort of 20 individuals with de novo FBXO11 variants, major structural malformations were notably absent; structural findings were restricted to cleft palate/lip or bifid uvula (3/20) and minor skeletal anomalies, without complex congenital heart defects or limb-reduction deficiencies.

evidence.text: In a prospective trio whole-genome sequencing cohort of 50 fetuses with prenatally detected structural malformations, one causative sequence variant was identified in FBXO11, showing that rare prenatal structural anomalies can prompt sequencing discovery, though complex CHDs and limb-reduction deficiencies were not highlighted as hallmark recurrences.

source.title: Whole‐genome sequencing in prenatally detected congenital malformations: prospective cohort study in clinical setting
source.quote: Causative sequence variants were identified in 12 genes: FGFR3 (n = 2), ACTA1 (n = 1), CDH2 (n = 1), COL1A2 (n = 1), DHCR7 (n = 1), EYA1 (n = 1), FBXO11 (n = 1), FRAS1 (n = 1), L1CAM (n = 1), OFD1 (n = 1), PDHA1 (n = 1) and SOX9 (n = 1).

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact phenotypic characterization of the prenatal FBXO11 case reported in fetal structural anomaly sequencing cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether prenatal ascertainment identifies severe internal organ defects (such as renal, pulmonary, or specific cardiac anomalies) that might be underrepresented in postnatal neurodevelopmental cohorts will define the absolute boundary of phenotypic severity.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact prevalence and anatomical breakdown of minor cardiac anomalies (such as bicuspid aortic valve or ASD/VSD) across all international FBXO11 registries?
new_directions.rationale: Differentiating common benign/minor cardiac defects (e.g., bicuspid aortic valve) from complex cyanotic or conotruncal congenital heart defects will refine formal cardiac screening guidelines for newly diagnosed FBXO11 patients.
